title: Ship Navigation Bridge and Workstations
description: Test your understanding of bridge layout, navigation equipment, communication systems, emergency equipment, sensor integration and practical bridge operations.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a ship's navigation bridge?
options: To control navigation, monitor the vessel and coordinate bridge operations
To store cargo documentation and spare equipment
To perform engine maintenance and fuel treatment
To accommodate the ship's emergency generator
questions.explanation: The bridge is the vessel's main navigation and command centre, where the bridge team monitors and controls the ship.

questions.question: Why are bridge wings particularly useful during berthing operations?
options: They provide a clear view along the ship's sides and toward the berth
They contain the vessel's main radio transmitters
They provide access to the cargo holds
They increase the range of the ship's radar
questions.explanation: Bridge wings allow the master, pilot or officer to observe the ship's side, berth, tugs and mooring operations.

questions.question: Which bridge instrument normally provides the vessel's true heading?
options: Gyrocompass
Echo sounder
Speed log
EPIRB
questions.explanation: The gyrocompass normally provides a true-north heading reference to the bridge and connected navigation systems.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an echo sounder?
options: To measure the water depth beneath the vessel
To measure the vessel's speed through the water
To identify nearby ships
To transmit distress alerts
questions.explanation: The echo sounder transmits sound pulses toward the seabed and measures the return time to determine water depth.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of an EPIRB?
options: To transmit a distress alert and help rescuers locate the vessel
To provide routine communication with VTS
To display the vessel's planned route
To measure wind direction
questions.explanation: An EPIRB sends a distress alert and identifying information through satellite systems to support search and rescue.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the relationship between radar and ECDIS?
options: Radar detects actual echoes, while ECDIS displays chart and sensor information
Radar and ECDIS always show identical information
ECDIS detects targets while radar provides official charts
Both systems depend entirely on AIS transmissions
questions.explanation: Radar detects reflected energy from real targets, while ECDIS displays electronic chart data integrated with navigation sensors.

questions.question: Why should AIS target information be checked against radar?
options: AIS data may be incorrect, outdated or unavailable
Radar can identify every target's cargo and destination
AIS only works while the vessel is alongside
Radar automatically corrects AIS identity information
questions.explanation: AIS depends on transmitted and manually entered data. Radar provides an independent means of detecting and monitoring targets.

questions.question: What is the main operational purpose of the conning position?
options: To provide essential information and controls for directing the vessel
To store paper charts and publications
To monitor machinery-space bilges
To test the emergency generator
questions.explanation: The conning position provides heading, speed, rudder, propulsion and other information needed to direct the vessel.

questions.question: Which information is normally supplied by a speed log?
options: Vessel speed and sometimes distance travelled
Geographical position and time
Water depth and seabed type
Wind direction and atmospheric pressure
questions.explanation: A speed log measures speed through the water or over the ground, depending on its design, and may also calculate distance.

questions.question: What is the main function of a radar SART?
options: To help rescuers locate survival craft by producing a distinctive radar response
To transmit routine weather reports
To display navigational warnings on ECDIS
To activate the ship's general alarm
questions.explanation: A radar SART responds to radar signals and produces a recognizable pattern on the rescuing vessel's radar display.

questions.question: The ECDIS position suddenly shifts several hundred metres, but radar ranges and visual bearings remain consistent with the previous position. What should the officer do first?
options: Treat the displayed position as unreliable and verify it using independent methods
Alter course immediately to return the ship symbol to the planned route
Assume the radar and visual bearings are incorrect
Disable all ECDIS alarms and continue
questions.explanation: A sudden position jump may indicate a GNSS or sensor error. The officer should verify the vessel's position before taking navigational action.

questions.question: The gyrocompass heading supplied to radar and ECDIS is incorrect. Which consequence is most likely?
options: Radar bearings, overlays and displayed target vectors may become misleading
The echo sounder will display an incorrect depth
The EPIRB will activate automatically
The speed log will stop measuring distance
questions.explanation: Incorrect heading input can affect radar orientation, target calculations, ECDIS presentation and other connected systems.

questions.question: During berthing, the master is using a bridge-wing control station. Which information is most important to verify before relying on the controls?
options: That steering, engine and thruster controls are correctly transferred and responding
That the NAVTEX receiver is printing messages
That the EPIRB hydrostatic release is valid
That the chart catalogue is updated
questions.explanation: Before manoeuvring from a wing station, the operator must verify that control has been transferred and that propulsion, steering and thrusters respond correctly.

questions.question: An AIS target shows a vessel proceeding at 12 knots, while radar plotting indicates that the target is nearly stationary. What is the best response?
options: Treat the information as conflicting and verify the target using radar, visual observation and communication
Use AIS because its digital information is always more accurate
Use radar only and switch off AIS
Assume the target has an equipment exemption
questions.explanation: Conflicting information must be investigated. AIS may contain delayed or incorrect data, while radar tracking may also be affected by errors.

questions.question: Why should the magnetic compass remain available when a gyrocompass is fitted?
options: It provides an independent heading reference if the gyro or electrical supply fails
It automatically corrects GPS errors
It supplies speed data to ARPA
It replaces the echo sounder in shallow water
questions.explanation: The magnetic compass is an independent system and can provide heading information following gyro or power failure.

questions.question: The bridge team reduces screen brightness excessively during night navigation. What is the main risk?
options: Important chart, radar or alarm information may become difficult to detect
The radar transmitter may overheat
The ship's heading will become inaccurate
The EPIRB battery will discharge
questions.explanation: Night lighting must preserve night vision while keeping essential displays, controls and alarms readable.

questions.question: A radar target is visible, but no corresponding AIS target appears. What should the officer conclude?
options: The radar echo may still represent a genuine target that is not transmitting AIS
The radar echo must be false because all ships transmit AIS
The target is automatically required to keep clear
The radar should be switched to standby
questions.explanation: Not every target carries or correctly operates AIS. Radar and visual observation remain essential.

questions.question: The vessel's echo sounder indicates rapidly decreasing depth, while the planned route and ECDIS position appear normal. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Investigate immediately by checking position, charted depths, under-keel clearance and independent information
Ignore the echo sounder because ECDIS is the primary system
Increase speed to pass the shallow area more quickly
Reduce the safety contour until the alarm clears
questions.explanation: Unexpected depth changes may indicate position error, shoaling water or equipment problems and require immediate verification.

questions.question: Why is a bridge workstation designed so essential information is visible from the operator's normal position?
options: To reduce workload, movement and loss of situational awareness
To allow one person to replace the entire bridge team
To remove the requirement for bridge windows
To prevent equipment from receiving sensor data
questions.explanation: Good ergonomic design reduces distraction and enables the operator to monitor the vessel and surrounding environment efficiently.

questions.question: A bridge alarm repeatedly sounds and is silenced without identifying its cause. Why is this unsafe?
options: The alarm may indicate a developing navigational or equipment failure that remains unresolved
Silencing an alarm permanently damages the radar antenna
The magnetic compass will become unreliable
The vessel will automatically alter course
questions.explanation: Alarms should be acknowledged, understood and acted upon. Silencing them without investigation may hide an unsafe condition.
